chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"If a man is certain that he missed one rak'ah of the prayer, having prostrated two prostrations and missed the bowing, he restarts the prayer."

key_terms.رَكْعَةً: A unit of prayer consisting of standing, bowing, and prostrating

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they realize they missed the ruku' but completed the sajda in their prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *ibtida'* (restarting) when a fundamental pillar like ruku' is omitted after the completion of the subsequent prostrations, distinguishing it from cases where the error is caught earlier. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the structural integrity of the rak'ah, ensuring that the sequence of worship remains valid by requiring a fresh start rather than simple correction when a major component is lost. This specific scenario highlights the meticulous attention to detail in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of obligatory acts within the prayer.
